channel.title: Looking for greenlight
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Looking for greenlight" - Can you tell me if this is a good idea or not. I'm looking for a greenlight so I can post this SCP.

item.title: Re: Looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hi author!

Here's the crit
here it be

Let me start off by saying that I do see the humor in how weird the basics of this concept are. The imagery of infectious hummingbirds is compelling.

However, I don't see this concept working as is. SCP articles are typically stories disguised as descriptive files. What you have here is a fairly straightforward "Monster Manual" entry, in which you present an idea for a creature and leave it at that. While that may have been a popular approach in the earlier days of the site, I think you'll find that things have progressed somewhat.

It's important to think about the story that your anomaly can tell, moreso even than the details of your anomaly's effects. I would recommend starting with a narrative you find interesting and then building an anomaly around it instead of vice versa. While you're at it, I'd also recommend checking out some Series VI skips just to get an idea of how story-driven most modern articles are.

Have a good day!

item.title: Looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): None

Page Layout (Optional): A normal SCP article with a long description short addendum and clear containment procedures.

Elevator Pitch: An infection caused by a fictional strain of hummingbirds.

Central Narrative: A microscopic hummingbird egg instance that infects a person and has three very deadly stages that include taking over the person's throat. cutting the vocal cords and veins in the neck. Then damaging the core parts of the brain then killing the infected person. Then breaking the person's jaw and flying out. Then laying new eggs. The eggs stay airborne for 30 days. The stages last over 4-6 months and it is classified as a Keter SCP. Here is the draft http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/sogn67893
